chapter: The band, its players and singers
title: Lester Young leaving: not fired but drafted
summary: Basie denies that he fired Lester over a missed Friday the 13th recording, saying Lester and Jo Jones both went into the Army.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: : All right, so let's get Hershel of the original sound. Did you ever -- who comes along next after Lester, 1940, I think Lester -- why did Lester --
Went into the Army. That's an (inaudible)

Well, what I read and this is back then in the newspaper in 1940, I have a news clipping from 1940. It's in New York Age. I will show it to you, and it says that Lester -- that you fired Lester from the band.
I will read you what it said, okay. He wasn't fired.
Lester went to the Army and then when Lester came out of the Army, Lester said that he would try a little thing of his own.

Okay. What was in the newspaper was that you had a recording, Lester didn't show up and you fired him and Lester said he didn't show up because the recording date was December 13th on a Friday and Friday, the 13th was no day for making music. Now, that's all I can say, is what I read.

No, any recording date we ever had that anybody we had showed up unless they were sick or something like that. I think that -- I don't know what happened to Hershel or whoever it was that they couldn't make it and Chu Berry filled in, but just only for that day.
I am going to bring this for you. I will just show it to you.
You don't have to show it to me. You have told me. I mean, I'm not worried about that at all, but this is not so.
So he of his own accord went into the Army. I mean, not of his own accord --
No, no. Jo Jones He and JoJo both.
They both went in the Army.
